t.7.51.1: Having spent that night there on the Gomatī, Lakṣmaṇa, the delight of the Raghus, rose again at dawn and then set out.
t.7.51.2: Then, when midday had come, the great chariot-warrior entered Ayodhyā, filled with jewels and thronged with joyful and well-nourished people.
t.7.51.3: But Saumitri, though exceedingly wise, sank into the deepest dejection, thinking: “When I have gone and come before Rāma's feet, what shall I say?”
t.7.51.4: As he was reflecting thus, the king's supremely magnificent palace, gleaming like the moon, came into view before him.
t.7.51.5: But that best of men, having alighted at the door of the king's palace, entered unhindered, with his face cast down and his mind dejected.
t.7.51.6: Seeing Rāghava seated dejected upon his excellent seat, he beheld his elder brother before him with eyes filled with tears.
t.7.51.7: Lakṣmaṇa, dejected in spirit, clasped his feet, and with joined palms, fully composed, he spoke in a sorrowful voice.
t.7.51.9: Do not grieve, O tiger among men; such is the course of Time. For those like you, endowed with strength of character and wisdom, do not grieve.
t.7.51.8: Honoring the noble one's command, I left Janaka's daughter on the bank of the Gaṅgā, as directed, at the auspicious hermitage of Vālmīki, and I have come back, O hero, to wait upon your feet.
t.7.51.10: All accumulations end in depletion, all elevations end in falling, unions end in separation, and life ends in death.
t.7.51.11: For you, O Kākutstha, are able by your own self to conquer yourself with the mind alone, and all the worlds as well; how much more, then, a sorrow such as this?
t.7.51.12: Bulls among men such as you do not lose their composure in matters like these, O king, the very cause for which Maithilī was abandoned out of fear of public censure.
t.7.51.13: So you, O tiger among men, well composed through fortitude, cast off this feeble thought, and do not give yourself over to grief.
t.7.51.14: Thus addressed by the great-souled Lakṣmaṇa, Kākutstha spoke with supreme affection to Saumitri, who was devoted to his friends.
t.7.51.15: It is just as you say, O Lakṣmaṇa, best of men; and I am well pleased, O hero, with your counsel to me on what must be done.
t.7.51.16: Gentle one, contentment has been brought about and my anguish has been dispelled; by your very sweet words I have been consoled, O Lakṣmaṇa.
